classification.difficultyReason: Subtract male students from the total before forming and simplifying the male-to-female ratio, then distinguish that comparison from the male fraction of the whole.

content.prompt: The number of students enrolled at a school is 1200. Of these, 625 are male.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the ratio of the number of male students to the number of female students? Express your ratio in simplest form.

answer.worked:
Number of female students $=1200-625=575$.

Divide both ratio terms by their HCF, $25$.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Male students : female students}&=625:575\\\text{Male students : female students}&=(625\div25):(575\div25)\\\text{Male students : female students}&=25:23\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: What fraction of the school population is male?

answer.worked:
Write the number of male students over the total number of students, then simplify.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Fraction male}&=\frac{625}{1200}\\\text{Fraction male}&=\frac{625\div25}{1200\div25}\\\text{Fraction male}&=\frac{25}{48}\end{align*}$$
